identity.title: Learning Human-Robot Collaboration via Heterogeneous-Agent Lyapunov Policy Optimization

problem.claim: How to stabilize decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning for human–robot collaboration across diverse human behaviors and contexts.

gap.claim: Heterogeneity creates a rationality gap between decentralized policy updates and cooperative joint optimization, while independent policy-gradient updates may oscillate or diverge in the resulting general-sum game.

contributions.claim: Proposes HALO, which enforces Lyapunov-based contraction in policy-parameter space to stabilize decentralized MARL.
Uses optimal quadratic projections to rectify decentralized gradients and monotonically contract the rationality gap.
Positions Lyapunov certification as a tool for stabilizing decentralized policy learning, distinct from Lyapunov-based safe RL focused on state or trajectory constraints.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors' stated distinction is applying Lyapunov certification to decentralized policy-learning stability in heterogeneous-agent MARL, rather than to constrained state or trajectory safety.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that simulations and real-world humanoid-robot experiments show improved generalization and robustness in collaborative corner cases under certified stability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Diverse human behaviors and contexts motivate MARL for more generalizable and resilient HRC.
Human–robot heterogeneity induces a rationality gap and turns learning into a general-sum differentiable game vulnerable to oscillation or divergence.
HALO stabilizes decentralized learning through Lyapunov contraction and quadratic gradient projection.
The framework is distinguished from Lyapunov-based safe RL by targeting policy-learning stability rather than state or trajectory constraints.
Simulated and real-world humanoid-robot experiments are reported to improve generalization and robustness in corner cases.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly separates policy-learning stability from state or trajectory safety, then aligns its method with that distinction.

lessons.interpretation: Separating neighboring objectives can make a technical contribution's scope and mechanism easier to evaluate.
lessons.application: When introducing a stability or safety method, define the controlled object, certification target, and contrast with the closest similarly named approach.
lessons.exception: This framing is less useful when the work genuinely addresses the neighboring objectives jointly or when the comparison lacks a meaningful shared mechanism.

unknowns: The abstract gives no quantitative metrics, baselines, task details, or experimental conditions for the reported improvements.
The extent to which monotonic rationality-gap contraction translates to generalization or robustness is not quantified in the abstract.
The abstract does not state formal theorem assumptions or proof details for the Lyapunov certification.
